ecological_question: Across neighboring Palmer Archipelago breeding islands, is penguin functional differentiation generated mainly by species turnover, or does a persistent within-species island phenotype remain after restricting to Adelie penguins?

three_year_hypotheses.H1_turnover: Archipelago-scale morphology-to-island predictability is dominated by species composition rather than persistent within-species island morphology.
three_year_hypotheses.H2_persistent_island: Persistent Adelie island phenotypes should produce fixed island effects after controlling sex, year, laying date and clutch completion.
three_year_hypotheses.H3_temporal_reassembly: Temporally labile colony states should produce island-by-year structure and reversals of pairwise island contrasts.
three_year_hypotheses.H4_cross_year_transfer: Persistent island phenotypes should classify held-out-year Adelie individuals above the one-third balanced-accuracy reference.

longterm_primary_question: Does long-term functional change on Antarctic breeding islands occur mainly through changes in species composition and abundance rather than inferred within-species morphological change?

longterm_rules.missing_species_record: exclude island-year; do not silently convert to zero
longterm_rules.primary_between_year_transition: same contributing site coverage in both years

interpretation_boundaries: No evolutionary local-adaptation claim from these observational data.
No individual-plasticity claim from island-by-year structural trait differences because different adults were sampled.
Body mass is condition-sensitive and is reported separately from structural traits.
Blood stable isotopes integrate pre-breeding foraging and are not local summer island-foraging measurements.
Community-weighted historical morphology initially uses fixed species trait centroids; it quantifies assembly-driven functional change, not historical trait evolution.
